summary: Scalp discomfort is prevalent and associated with impaired quality of life and sleep disturbance. title: ALE meta-analysis of cognitive control, motivation, and effort in schizophrenia and mood disorders: implications for multidimensional apathy.

title: Sensitivity to Rule-Outcome Conflict in Social Decision Making: A Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study.
summary: Social rules shape expectations, but actual outcomes may diverge. This functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study examined how rule-formation context and individual differences in sensitivity to rule-outcome conflicts are associated with social decision-making. Seventy-nine participants underwent fMRI while completing a modified Ultimatum Game as responders; 65 participants were included in the final analysis. title: Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors of Tandem Spinal Stenosis.
summary: Tandem spinal stenosis (TSS) is a complex, multi-level degenerative condition that is notoriously underdiagnosed due to overlapping symptoms and diagnostic masking. summary: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of death and disability as well as impaired cognition and sleep-wake abnormalities. summary: To compare MSDA Score and pathway scores between patients treated with ocrelizumab and natalizumab in real-world MS population. title: Diagnosis and surgical management of a type IVb dermoid sinus between the parietal and occipital bones in a young cat.
summary: A dermoid sinus is a congenital, tubular skin defect caused by incomplete separation of the skin and nervous system during embryonic development. summary: Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is the most common monogenic cause of cerebral small vessel disease, yet its clinical management remains poorly harmonized across Europe. title: A Novel DHX9 Variant Was Identified in a Patient With Developmental Delay, Facial Dysmorphism and Seizure.

title: Cortical Macro- and Microstructural Alterations in Multiple System Atrophy and Their Clinical Correlates.

summary: Multisensory environments (MSEs) are valuable therapeutic spaces for relaxation and stress relief, yet high costs and physical infrastructure limit accessibility.
